output.text: I am the rook, and I have spent my life along the edge of the board, where the corners are sharp and the silence is deep. I am the rook, and I have watched the knight leap—three squares this way, two that—like a rumor that refuses to stay still. I envied that chaos, the way he danced over the squares like he owned the whole game. I thought my straight lines were prison, my rigid paths a sentence. But then, one afternoon, the light caught the edge of the board just right, and I saw my shadow stretch—long, unbroken, true. I realized: my strength is not in the leap, but in the line. I am the rook, and I am the edge of the board. And in that straight line, I found pride. Not in what I could not be, but in what I am.
